note: Corps of Engineers campground on an open-wooded point of Stockton Lake. Sites 7-46 have electric; sites 1-6 and 47-66 are basic. The sites around the rim of the point sit on open ground just above the water. Drinking water and electric are on only from Apr 16 to Sep 29; in the shoulder seasons (Mar 15 to Apr 15, Oct 1 to Nov 30) amenities are reduced. Camping only, no day use. Boat ramp and beach just outside the entrance. --Claude
summary: Read on rec.gov: 63 sites (37 with 30A electric, 26 basic), $20/$28 in the Apr 16-Sep 29 reservation season, showers/flush/vault/dump/water. Stored count 74 -> 63 (catalog); stored hookups.water true cleared (no site states a water hookup). Waterfront lead UP lakeview -> lakefront (counted). Pin is rec.gov's facility point about 740 m from the sites - move flagged. Winter status and shoulder-season rates are not on rec.gov.
flags: WATERFRONT LEAD UP (stored lakeview, no stored evidence): on the 0.33 m/px leaf-off frames the campground covers a point with scattered trees over mown ground, and the lake is drawn down (a bare band 10-20 m wide rings the point, so distances to today's water are upper bounds). Electric sites on the north rim: 15 about 20 m from the pool-level edge / 30 m from the water, 13 about 33 m, 17 about 25 m, 19 about 25 m, 10 about 20 m, 21 about 30 m; on the west rim 23, 25, 27 about 35-40 m to the pool edge (50-55 m to the drawn-down water); basic sites on the south-west lobe 63 about 17 m, 61 about 20-35 m, 59 about 25 m, 57 about 20 m; east side 09 and 11 about 35-45 m. Nothing but grass and a few trunks between these pads and the shore; no road or day use between. At least ten RV sites (six of them electric) on an open apron within 50 m. Supports LAKEFRONT. rec.gov carries no Proximity to Water value on any site, and no site photos were read.

PIN MOVE: stored 37.5258,-93.8094 is rec.gov's facility point. The catalog's 63 site coordinates centre on 37.52302,-93.81699 and match the pads on imagery; the stored pin is about 740 m east-north-east of that centre and about 400 m from the nearest site (01). Proposed new pin 37.5230,-93.8170.

HOOKUPS: stored water=true (derived from note prose) cleared to unknown. No campsite record carries a water hookup value; the facility notice says 'Drinking water and electric hookups are available during the reservation season'. Ruark Bluff East, the sister park, states water hookup 'No' and a community fill-up. Likely shared spigots here too (potable_water written true) but rec.gov does not say it for this park. Electric is 30 amp on all 37 electric sites; no 50 amp.

SITES: rec.gov prose says 74 campsites; the catalog lists 63 individual sites (numbers 01-66 without 22, 24, 26) plus the Ruark Bluff Group Camp (electric, $180, plotted at 37.53013,-93.80851, about 1.1 km north-east of the sites). Written 63.

WINTER / SEASON (not written - unknown): rec.gov gives the reservation season (Apr 16-Sep 29) and says the shoulder seasons Mar 15-Apr 15 and Oct 1-Nov 30 run with reduced amenities. It does not say whether the park is gated Dec 1-Mar 14, what is charged in the shoulder seasons (the rate table has only the peak season), or whether shoulder-season camping is first come first served. Ruark Bluff East's notice says open year-round; this park's has no such line. A question for the park (417-637-5279) or project office (417-276-3113). The USACE lake page was not read.
FEES: the rate table also has one unnamed $30 template that I could not tie to a site type; $20/$28 written from the named site types.
PHONE (none stored; apply.py does not write it): rec.gov facility phone 417-637-5279 (park), project office 417-276-3113.
